title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 9. Beholding the Site of the Great Rasa Dance
html:
Krishnadasa shows the Lord the place where Varuna carried off Nanda, the Brahma-kunda, the ashoka grove and the site of the rasa dance; Gaurachandra, shining forth, reveals the festival of the rasa with His devotees; the brahmana continues his account — the song at the Vamshivata, Krishna's disappearance with one gopi, His return and the great rasa on the bank of the Yamuna; hearing it, the Lord manifests Radha and Krishna within Himself

Verse 1

अत्रैव यमुनानीरे द्वादशीव्रतकर्शितः।
वरुणेन हृतो नन्दः कृष्णदर्शनकाम्यया॥१॥

atraiva yamunānīre dvādaśīvratakarśitaḥ|
varuṇena hṛto nandaḥ kṛṣṇadarśanakāmyayā||1||

atra — here; eva — indeed; yamuna-nire — in the waters of the Yamuna; dvadashi-vrata-karshitah — emaciated by the vow of the Dvadashi; varunena — by Varuna; hritah — was carried off; nandah — Nanda; krishna-darshana-kamyaya — out of the desire to see Krishna.

1"Here in the waters of the Yamuna, Varuna, longing to see Krishna, carried off Nanda, who was worn thin by the vow of the Dvadashi1.

Verse 2

ज्ञात्वा ततोऽपि भगवान् स्वयं पितरमानयत्।
ब्रह्मकुण्डे मज्जयित्वा स्वजनं ब्रह्मलोकतः॥२॥

jñātvā tato'pi bhagavān svayaṁ pitaramānayat|
brahmakuṇḍe majjayitvā svajanaṁ brahmalokataḥ||2||

jnatva — knowing (this); tatah — from there; api — too; bhagavan — the Lord; svayam — Himself; pitaram — His father; anayat — brought back; brahma-kunde — in the Brahma-kunda; majjayitva — having made bathe; sva-janam — His own people; brahma-lokatah — from the world of Brahman.

2Learning of this, the Lord Himself brought His father back from there; and then, having made His own people bathe in the Brahma-kunda, from the world of Brahman2

Verse 3

आनिनाय पुनर्वृन्दारण्यं गोपकुलं विभुः।
तं कुण्डं परमं रम्यं पश्य कृष्ण सुदुर्लभम्॥३॥

ānināya punarvṛndāraṇyaṁ gopakulaṁ vibhuḥ|
taṁ kuṇḍaṁ paramaṁ ramyaṁ paśya kṛṣṇa sudurlabham||3||

aninaya — brought; punah — back; vrindaranyam — to Vrindavana; gopa-kulam — the clan of cowherds; vibhuh — the Almighty; tam — that; kundam — pond; paramam — supremely; ramyam — lovely; pashya — behold; krishna — O Krishna; su-durlabham — very hard to attain.

3the Almighty brought the cowherd clan back to Vrindavana. Behold this pond, O Krishna3 — supremely lovely and very hard to attain.

Verse 4

अशोककाननं रम्यं ब्रह्मकुण्डस्य चोत्तरे।
श्रीराधया सह कृष्णो यत्र क्रीडति पश्य तत्॥४॥

aśokakānanaṁ ramyaṁ brahmakuṇḍasya cottare|
śrīrādhayā saha kṛṣṇo yatra krīḍati paśya tat||4||

ashoka-kananam — the grove of ashoka trees; ramyam — lovely; brahma-kundasya — of the Brahma-kunda; cha — and; uttare — to the north; shri-radhaya — with Sri Radha; saha — together; krishnah — Krishna; yatra — where; kridati — sports; pashya — behold; tat — that.

4And to the north of the Brahma-kunda is a lovely grove of ashoka trees, where Krishna sports with Sri Radha; behold it.

Verse 5

कार्त्तिकीपूर्णिमायां तु देवदेवेश्वरो हरिः।
चकार रासं गोपीभिर्यत्र श्रीश्यामसुन्दरः॥५॥

kārttikīpūrṇimāyāṁ tu devadeveśvaro hariḥ|
cakāra rāsaṁ gopībhiryatra śrīśyāmasundaraḥ||5||

karttiki-purnimayam — on the full moon of Karttika; tu — and; deva-deva-ishvarah — the Lord of the lords of the gods; harih — Hari; chakara — performed; rasam — the rasa dance; gopibhih — with the gopis; yatra — where; shri-shyamasundarah — Sri Shyamasundara.

5Here, on the full moon of Karttika, Hari, the Lord of the lords of the gods, Sri Shyamasundara, danced the rasa with the gopis4."

Verse 6

तदैव रसिकाग्रणीः स खलु गौरचन्द्रो हरि-
र्महामणिनिभद्युतिः प्रकटमेव व्यक्तीभवन्।
स रासरसताण्डवैर्विविधरम्यवेशोज्ज्वलै-
रत्नोक्षितसुलक्षितैर्जयति भक्तवर्गैः प्रभुः॥६॥

tadaiva rasikāgraṇīḥ sa khalu gauracandro hari-
rmahāmaṇinibhadyutiḥ prakaṭameva vyaktībhavan|
sa rāsarasatāṇḍavairvividharamyaveśojjvalai-
ratnokṣitasulakṣitairjayati bhaktavargaiḥ prabhuḥ||6||

tada — then; eva — at once; rasika-agranih — the foremost of connoisseurs of rasa; sah — He; khalu — indeed; gaurachandrah — Gaurachandra; harih — Hari; maha-mani-nibha-dyutih — with a radiance like a great gem; prakatam — openly; eva — indeed; vyaktibhavan — becoming manifest; sah — He; rasa-rasa-tandavaih — with wild dances in the rasa of the rasa dance; vividha-ramya-vesha-ujjvalaih — resplendent in various lovely attire; ratna-ukshita-su-lakshitaih — finely marked as if sprinkled with jewels; jayati — triumphs; bhakta-vargaih — with the hosts of devotees; prabhuh — the Lord.

6And at once Hari, Gaurachandra, the foremost of those who relish rasa, radiant like a great gem, plainly revealed Himself: with His devotees, wildly dancing in the rasa of the rasa dance, resplendent in many lovely garments as though sprinkled with jewels — the Lord triumphs!

Verse 7

प्रफुल्लमधुरद्युतिः सरसरम्यवृन्दावनं
वसन्तवनमारुतैः प्रकटयन् स रासोत्सवैः।
सुरम्यमपि किं ब्रुवे सकलमेव रासस्थलं
स गोपीजनवल्लभो मदनगर्वखर्वो बभौ॥७॥

praphullamadhuradyutiḥ sarasaramyavṛndāvanaṁ
vasantavanamārutaiḥ prakaṭayan sa rāsotsavaiḥ|
suramyamapi kiṁ bruve sakalameva rāsasthalaṁ
sa gopījanavallabho madanagarvakharvo babhau||7||

praphulla-madhura-dyutih — with a blossoming, sweet radiance; sa-rasa-ramya-vrindavanam — lovely Vrindavana full of rasa; vasanta-vana-marutaih — with the spring breezes of the forest; prakatayan — manifesting; sah — He; rasa-utsavaih — with the festivals of the rasa dance; su-ramyam — most lovely; api — indeed; kim — what; bruve — shall I say; sakalam — the whole; eva — indeed; rasa-sthalam — site of the rasa dance; sah — He; gopi-jana-vallabhah — the beloved of the gopis; madana-garva-kharvah — who humbles the pride of Madana; babhau — shone.

7With a sweet radiance like a flower in bloom He made manifest lovely Vrindavana, full of rasa, with the spring breezes of its woods and the festivals of the rasa. What shall I say of the whole site of the rasa, already so lovely? There He shone — the beloved of the gopis, who humbles the pride of Madana5.

Verse 8

दृष्ट्वा विप्रस्तथाभूतं तथापीश्वरमायया।
वृतं स दर्शयामास पूर्वलीलास्थलीं शुभाम्॥८॥

dṛṣṭvā viprastathābhūtaṁ tathāpīśvaramāyayā|
vṛtaṁ sa darśayāmāsa pūrvalīlāsthalīṁ śubhām||8||

drishtva — having seen; viprah — the brahmana; tatha-bhutam — (Him) in that state; tatha api — even so; ishvara-mayaya — by the maya of the Lord; vritam — (Him) veiled; sah — he; darshayam asa — showed; purva-lila-sthalim — the site of the former pastime; shubham — auspicious.

8The brahmana saw Him so; and yet he did not recognise Him, for the Lord had veiled Himself by His yogamaya6 — and he went on showing Him the auspicious places of the former pastimes.

Verse 9

अतस्तं पश्य गोविन्दो वंशीवटसमीपतः।
स्थितो जगौ कामबीजं गोपीजनविमोहनम्॥९॥

atastaṁ paśya govindo vaṁśīvaṭasamīpataḥ|
sthito jagau kāmabījaṁ gopījanavimohanam||9||

atah — next; tam — that (place); pashya — behold; govindah — Govinda; vamshivata-samipatah — near the Vamshivata; sthitah — standing; jagau — sang; kama-bijam — the kama-bija; gopi-jana-vimohanam — which enchants the gopis.

9"Now behold that place over there: here, by the Vamshivata7, Govinda stood and sang the kama-bija8 that enchants the gopis.

Verse 10

श्रुत्वा सुललितं गानं गोप्यस्तत्र समाययुः।
ताभ्यः प्रेममदाद्बाह्यं कृष्णो धर्ममशिक्षयत्॥१०॥

śrutvā sulalitaṁ gānaṁ gopyastatra samāyayuḥ|
tābhyaḥ premamadādbāhyaṁ kṛṣṇo dharmamaśikṣayat||10||

shrutva — hearing; su-lalitam — the charming; ganam — song; gopyah — the gopis; tatra — there; samayayuh — gathered; tabhyah — to them; premam — love; adat — gave; bahyam — the outward; krishnah — Krishna; dharmam — dharma; ashikshayat — taught.

10Hearing that charming song, the gopis gathered here. Krishna gave them love, while outwardly He instructed them in dharma9.

Verse 11

तासां विशुद्धसत्त्वं च भावदाता च प्रेमदः।
चकार रासमप्यत्र कृष्णो योगेश्वरेश्वरः॥११॥

tāsāṁ viśuddhasattvaṁ ca bhāvadātā ca premadaḥ|
cakāra rāsamapyatra kṛṣṇo yogeśvareśvaraḥ||11||

tasam — to them; vishuddha-sattvam — pure sattva; cha — and; bhava-data — the giver of bhava; cha — and; prema-dah — the giver of prema; chakara — performed; rasam — the rasa dance; api — also; atra — here; krishnah — Krishna; yoga-ishvara-ishvarah — the Lord of the lords of yoga.

11Giving them pure sattva10 and bhava, giving them prema, Krishna, the Lord of the lords of yoga, danced the rasa with them right here.

Verse 12

अत्र तं पश्य गौराङ्ग गोविन्दरसकौतुकी।
वृन्दावनाधिपत्यं च चकार रसवल्लभः॥१२॥

atra taṁ paśya gaurāṅga govindarasakautukī|
vṛndāvanādhipatyaṁ ca cakāra rasavallabhaḥ||12||

atra — here; tam — that (place); pashya — behold; gauranga — O Gauranga; govinda-rasa-kautuki — eager for the rasa of Govinda; vrindavana-adhipatyam — sovereignty over Vrindavana; cha — and; chakara — assumed; rasa-vallabhah — the Beloved of rasa.

12Behold this place, Gauranga, You who long for the rasa of Govinda: here the Beloved of rasa assumed sovereignty over Vrindavana.

Verse 13

एवं रासरसामोदी गोपीनां रागवृद्धये।
एकामादाय सहसा तिरोभूतोऽत्र पश्य तत्॥१३॥

evaṁ rāsarasāmodī gopīnāṁ rāgavṛddhaye|
ekāmādāya sahasā tirobhūto'tra paśya tat||13||

evam — thus; rasa-rasa-amodi — delighting in the rasa of the rasa dance; gopinam — of the gopis; raga-vriddhaye — to increase the passion; ekam — one; adaya — taking; sahasa — suddenly; tirobhutah — vanished; atra — here; pashya — behold; tat — that.

13So, delighting in the rasa of the dance, He suddenly vanished, taking one of them with Him11, to heighten the gopis' love; behold that place.

Verse 14

तस्याः सुचरितं केन वर्ण्यते श्रूयतेऽथवा।
यस्याः प्रेमपराधीनस्तां हि स्वाधीनभर्तृकाम्॥१४॥

tasyāḥ sucaritaṁ kena varṇyate śrūyate'thavā|
yasyāḥ premaparādhīnastāṁ hi svādhīnabhartṛkām||14||

tasyah — her; su-charitam — wondrous story; kena — by whom; varnyate — is described; shruyate — is heard; atha-va — or; yasyah — to whose; prema-paradhinah — subject to the love; tam — her; hi — indeed; svadhina-bhartrikam — who holds her lover in her power.

14Who could describe, or even hear in full, her wondrous story? He was subject to her love, she held her Beloved in her power — and yet her

Verse 15

तत्याज कौतुकी कृष्णः स्थितोऽस्याः सन्निधिं हसन्।
सापि कृष्णं न पश्यन्ती विह्वला तत्सखीजनाः॥१५॥

tatyāja kautukī kṛṣṇaḥ sthito'syāḥ sannidhiṁ hasan|
sāpi kṛṣṇaṁ na paśyantī vihvalā tatsakhījanāḥ||15||

tatyaja — abandoned; kautuki — playful; krishnah — Krishna; sthitah — staying (nearby); asyah — her; sannidhim — side; hasan — laughing; sa — she; api — too; krishnam — Krishna; na — not; pashyanti — seeing; vihvala — (was) distraught; tat-sakhi-janah — her friends.

15playful Krishna left, laughing, though He stayed close by. Not seeing Krishna, she was distraught; and her friends,

Verse 16

मिलिताः कृष्णजन्मादिलीलातन्मयतां ययुः।
गोप्यः प्रेमपराधीनास्तत्तद्रूपप्रकाशिकाम्॥१६॥

militāḥ kṛṣṇajanmādilīlātanmayatāṁ yayuḥ|
gopyaḥ premaparādhīnāstattadrūpaprakāśikām||16||

militah — gathering together; krishna-janma-adi-lila-tanmayatam — absorption in Krishna's pastimes beginning with His birth; yayuh — attained; gopyah — the gopis; prema-paradhinah — subject to love; tat-tad-rupa-prakashikam — which revealed each of those forms.

16gathering together — the gopis, subject to love — became absorbed in Krishna's pastimes from His birth onward, an absorption that revealed in them, one after another, His forms12.

Verse 17

ताभ्यः स्वविरहव्याधिपीडिताभ्यो निजां तनुम्।
प्रहसन् दर्शयामास कृष्णो नारायणः स्वयम्॥१७॥

tābhyaḥ svavirahavyādhipīḍitābhyo nijāṁ tanum|
prahasan darśayāmāsa kṛṣṇo nārāyaṇaḥ svayam||17||

tabhyah — to them; sva-viraha-vyadhi-piditabhyah — tormented by the sickness of separation from Him; nijam — His own; tanum — form; prahasan — smiling; darshayam asa — showed; krishnah — Krishna; narayanah — Narayana; svayam — Himself.

17To them, tormented by the sickness of separation, Krishna — Narayana Himself13 — smiling, showed His own form14.

Verse 18

ताभिः सम्मानितः कृष्णः परिहासे पराजितः।
रासं चकार धर्मज्ञो मण्डलीं परिकल्पयन्॥१८॥

tābhiḥ sammānitaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ parihāse parājitaḥ|
rāsaṁ cakāra dharmajño maṇḍalīṁ parikalpayan||18||

tabhih — by them; sammanitah — honoured; krishnah — Krishna; parihase — in banter; parajitah — defeated; rasam — the rasa dance; chakara — performed; dharma-jnah — the knower of dharma; mandalim — a circle; parikalpayan — forming.

18Honoured by them and defeated in their banter, Krishna, the knower of dharma, formed a circle and danced the rasa15.

Verse 19

विलासरसमाधुरीरसमदेन मत्तः किल
संनीय स्वबलाजनान् यमभगिनीतीरं हरिः।
प्रकाश्य बहुरूपतां जगदनङ्गसंमर्दनो
रराज व्रजसुन्दरीनिजभुजैस्तु बद्धः स्वयम्॥१९॥

vilāsarasamādhurīrasamadena mattaḥ kila
saṁnīya svabalājanān yamabhaginītīraṁ hariḥ|
prakāśya bahurūpatāṁ jagadanaṅgasaṁmardano
rarāja vrajasundarīnijabhujaistu baddhaḥ svayam||19||

vilasa-rasa-madhuri-rasa-madena — with the intoxication of the rasa of the sweetness of play; mattah — enraptured; kila — truly; sanniya — leading; sv-abala-janan — the fair women; yama-bhagini-tiram — to the bank of Yama's sister; harih — Hari; prakashya — manifesting; bahu-rupatam — multiplicity of forms; jagad-ananga-sammardanah — the crusher of Ananga (who conquers) the world; raraja — shone; vraja-sundari-nija-bhujaih — by the very arms of the beauties of Vraja; tu — and; baddhah — entwined; svayam — Himself.

19Truly, enraptured by the rasa of the sweetness of play, Hari led the fair women to the bank of Yama's sister16, and, manifesting many forms — He who crushes Ananga17, the conqueror of the world — He shone, Himself entwined in the arms of the beauties of Vraja."

Verse 20

श्रुत्वा रासविलासवैभवरसं श्रीगौरचन्द्रो हरिः
प्रेमोन्मादविभिन्नधैर्यनिवहो माधुर्यसारोज्ज्वलः।
राधाकृष्णं व्रजवधूगणैर्वेष्टितं संविभाव्य
प्राकट्यं तत् स्वात्मनि तयोर्दर्शयन् संबभौ स्म॥२०॥

śrutvā rāsavilāsavaibhavarasaṁ śrīgauracandro hariḥ
premonmādavibhinnadhairyanivaho mādhuryasārojjvalaḥ|
rādhākṛṣṇaṁ vrajavadhūgaṇairveṣṭitaṁ saṁvibhāvya
prākaṭyaṁ tat svātmani tayordarśayan saṁbabhau sma||20||

shrutva — having heard; rasa-vilasa-vaibhava-rasam — the rasa of the splendour of the rasa pastimes; shri-gaurachandrah — Sri Gaurachandra; harih — Hari; prema-unmada-vibhinna-dhairya-nivahah — His whole composure shattered by the madness of love; madhurya-sara-ujjvalah — resplendent with the essence of sweetness; radha-krishnam — Radha and Krishna; vraja-vadhu-ganaih — by the throngs of the women of Vraja; veshtitam — surrounded; samvibhavya — deeply contemplating; prakatyam — the manifestation; tat — that; sva-atmani — in His own self; tayoh — of the two; darshayan — displaying; sambabhau sma — shone forth.

20Hearing of the splendour of the rasa pastimes, Sri Gaurachandra Hari — all His composure shattered by the madness of love, resplendent with the essence of sweetness — deeply contemplated Radha and Krishna surrounded by the throngs of the women of Vraja, and, displaying the two of them within His own self, He shone forth18.

Thus ends the ninth sarga, "Beholding the Site of the Great Rasa Dance" (Maharasa-sthali-darshana), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The Dvadashi is the twelfth lunar day, which follows the Ekadashi fast. Nanda entered the Yamuna before the proper hour, and a servant of Varuna, lord of the waters, led him away; see Bhagavata Purana 10.28.
  2. Ibid. 10.28.16–17: Krishna had the cowherds plunge into the "lake of Brahman" and showed them His own abode.
  3. Krishnadasa addresses the Lord by the name of Krishna.
  4. The rasa dance is described in Bhagavata Purana 10.29–33; tradition places it on the autumn full moon of Karttika.
  5. Madana: the god of love (Kamadeva).
  6. Yogamaya is the Lord's internal, spiritual energy, by which He Himself conceals or reveals Himself in His pastimes (cf. Bhagavad-gita 7.25: "I am not manifest to all, being veiled by yogamaya"). It is not the external maya that deludes living beings; the Lord is never subject to that. The verse can also be understood otherwise: it was the brahmana who was under the Lord's maya, and so did not recognise Him.
  7. The Vamshivata: the banyan in Vrindavana beneath which Krishna played His flute.
  8. Kama-bija: the "seed of love," the secret syllable of a mantra addressed to Krishna; here, the calling of His flute.
  9. Cf. Bhagavata Purana 10.29.18–27: Krishna tells the gopis who have come to go back to their husbands and do their duty.
  10. Vishuddha-sattva: "pure being," the transcendent nature free from the gunas of matter, in which bhava awakens.
  11. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition, Sri Radha (cf. Bhagavata Purana 10.30.35–41).
  12. Bhagavata Purana 10.30.14–23: separated from Krishna, the gopis act out His pastimes, becoming like Him.
  13. "Narayana" here is a name of Krishna Himself, the Supreme Lord (cf. Bhagavata Purana 10.14.14); in Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching the Narayana of Vaikuntha is a manifestation of Krishna, not Krishna a manifestation of Narayana.
  14. Ibid. 10.32.2.
  15. Ibid. 10.32.17–22 (Krishna owns Himself the gopis' debtor) and 10.33.
  16. The Yamuna, sister of Yama, the god of death.
  17. Ananga ("the Bodiless"): the god of love.
  18. According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching, Sri Chaitanya is Radha and Krishna in one form.
